searchText: I pretty strongly against this change. I fear that it is going to lead to more bugs than it fixes, and the bugs it causes will be more subtle and harder to debug. I understand that some tooling expects the field to be present, but if the field is missing entirely then the tool fails hard and fast and fixing it should be pretty simple. If the field is present but *wrong*, then the tools will fail in bizarre ways. Also, if we continue to provide this field people will continue to use it rather than using the more correct receipt. If we are going to include it, we should have a very clear EOL policy for it and document that in the description. For example, "this field will be removed from clients sometime after 2022-01-01". (left comments on PR, which is probably a more appropriate place for discussion) <@!301186049323958275> re: being agianst the PR entirely, the challenge is that clients already implement this, so changing the spec won't fix things now I agree re: having a clear deprecation date. Does it make sense to say Shanghai? When it is unclear when Shanghai is? 🙂 It isn't: we need a fork this December because of the difficulty bomb Whether it includes anything beyond that is TBD, but everyone will need to update then There's still debate whether that is named shanghai, or like Muir Glacier, another two-word fork (in case no feature goes in just the bomb). Also unclear whether the merge will be named merge, or shanghai/cancun/etc. IMO we name it Shanghai even if just the bomb for clarity and we name The Merge, the Merge I would vote for "removed sometime after Shanghai". So people can rely on it being available in the Shanghai client, but not any client after. _if_ The Merge is ready before December, then maybe Shanghai just never goes live? Because you think 4-5 months is too soon for full deprecation? Why does the merge deserves its own name, but shanghai can be used for a non-feature work? 🙂 At the least we should change the behavior from what is in the PR. In my PR comment I made a recommendation on an alternative behavior that is at least not nearly as error prone as the behavior described in the PR. What that PR describes is a recipe for lots of problems. I think the community already associates "the merge" with "The Merge" If there's consistency regarding fork naming and timing, which I gather is your goal, then forks should just be named as the cities, no matter the content. As for Shanghai, IMO it just provides better clarity to say "Shanghai EOY" -> "The Merge" -> "Cancun" Anyway sorry for interrupting, this convo doesn't belong here I suppose. My personal opinion is that consistency is good in general, but I'm fine not being overly strict about it. Hence, I'm with with "The Merge" being a name, but it's not a hill I care to die on, though 🙂 Ok maybe one last thing: the difficulty bomb is a special one, especially considering the goal with merge (it will be gone). If there's no feature fork, only a "workaround" fork, then it makes sense following tradition and using some other two-word fork name for it, and not shanghai. Fair enough, <@!425279588009246720> ! I think this is probably something we can agree on on the next ACD? Or at least bring up As that feels like more a "quick fix" prior to the merge, and it seems to be the likely case given the sentiment on last ACD. Because if we want to do more than just a diff bomb delay in December, we basically need to start working on it now, and yeah, on the past ACD it seemed like the sentiment was somewhat against that. Not sure next ACD will be well populated, but definitely should be discussed there and not here 😅 👍 I'll add something to the /pm repo <@!301186049323958275> as for your original comment, I just don't think we can change it at this point We really *need* to change it. The current behavior is truly problematic. because all the client versions which went live for London this week use the "maxFee before mining, effectiveFee after" behavior Ugh. That is going to wreak havoc. Can any of them get a patch out? Even if the patch comes out immediately after London, that behavior is atrocious and will cause so much dev headache. Debugging problems when the behavior changes based on the time you call an API is a massive pain point for development. You'll end up with users having problems and when the dev goes to investigate they cannot reproduce. You also will have people probing behavior during development and coding against that probed behavior and then experiencing *different* behavior *sometimes* in production. It is just all around a really bad situation for any integration. The Geth team came up with that behavior, so IMO they would be the main people you'd have to convince to change it 😅
